title: Astrid and the Choir
premise: When the crown declares the Gift a plague and hunts its bearers, August Blackwood flees into the Thornfell mountains with a smuggler's knowledge and a hedge-witch's half-trained power. She falls in with the Choir, a ragged circle of hunted magicians hiding beneath an abandoned monastery, and discovers their secret: the king is not a tyrant but a vessel, bound decades ago by the entity now wearing his crown — the same entity that once bound August's vanished mentor. As the hunt closes in and the Choir fractures over whether to save the king or kill him, August learns her mentor's unbinding rite is the only way to free them both. In the frozen chapel where the binding was made, August pays the rite's price — her own Gift — unbinding the king and destroying the entity, then returns to the Choir powerless but unbroken, finding that the family that chose her never needed her magic at all.
about_author: Kestrel Thornbury is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent six years mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction, a trade that left her with a lifelong obsession with borders and the people who cross them illegally. She writes fantasy about outsiders, oaths, and the geography of belonging from a drafty farmhouse she refuses to heat properly on principle.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Ledger
chapters.summary: August Blackwood's POV. August guides contraband over the Thornfell passes, eking out a living since fleeing her mentor Ysolde years ago. When a routine delivery turns out to be a hunted Gift-bearer, August hides him from crown soldiers — and is seen using magic to do it. Emotional beat: guilt over the past curdling into fear for the future.

chapters.title: Proclamation at Millbrook Cross
chapters.summary: August's POV. The crown's edict is nailed to every door: the Gift is a plague; bearers will be culled. August watches a neighbor she's known all her life be dragged away. She burns her mentor's letters, packs her kit, and takes the deep roads north. Emotional beat: the shattering of home.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Keeps
chapters.summary: August's POV, with a brief interlude from hunted singer Tam Voss. Pursued through a blizzard, August is cornered at a shrine — and saved by Tam and the Choir, who have been shadowing her since Millbrook. They carry her to their hidden refuge beneath the ruined monastery of Candlemere. Emotional beat: wary relief, the first taste of not being alone.

chapters.title: The Choir of Candlemere
chapters.summary: August's POV. She meets the Choir: pragmatic leader Brannoc, healer Sef, twins Wren and Lark, and the boy Osk who cannot stop hearing the king's dreams. August learns the Choir's heresy — the king is a prisoner, not a tyrant. Emotional beat: skepticism warring with longing to belong.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Osk's POV. Through his unwanted connection, Osk shows August the king's mind: a man buried alive beneath an ancient entity called the Regent, which has ruled through him for thirty years. August recognizes the binding style — it is Ysolde's work. Emotional beat: horror and the vertigo of a rewritten past.

chapters.title: Lessons in Borrowed Fire
chapters.summary: August's POV. Brannoc trains August in the Choir's collaborative magic, which she resents after years of Ysolde's solitary discipline. A raid on a crown supply train goes wrong; August saves Wren at the cost of revealing her power's strange signature. Emotional beat: friction becoming trust.

chapters.title: The Hunter with the Kind Face
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Maren Vale's POV. Maren, who hunts Gift-bearers with genuine compassion, traces the signature from the supply raid. She interrogates August's old village and finds the burned letters — and one unburned page naming Candlemere. Emotional beat: the antagonist's terrible decency.

chapters.title: Ysolde's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: August's POV. Deciphering her mentor's letters, August learns Ysolde helped bind the king as a young woman — and spent her life trying to undo it before the Regent consumed her too. Her disappearance was not abandonment but flight. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: August's POV. The rite requires three things: the binder's bloodline or apprentice, a song the Choir alone can sing, and a price the caster chooses freely. Brannoc argues the price should be a life — the king's. August argues for salvation. Emotional beat: the Choir's first true fracture.

chapters.title: What Osk Hears in the Dark
chapters.summary: Osk's POV. The Regent has noticed Osk listening and begins speaking back, offering him power and showing him the Choir's destruction. Osk hides the contact, ashamed, and the entity learns Candlemere's location through him. Emotional beat: shame as a weapon turned inward.

chapters.title: Ash Wednesday Market
chapters.summary: August's POV. The Choir risks a winter town to buy components for the rite. August comes face to face with Maren Vale, who recognizes her but hesitates — and lets her go, troubled. Emotional beat: the enemy's doubt, and August's dangerous flicker of sympathy.

chapters.title: The Vote at Candlemere
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. The Choir votes on the king's fate: kill him and end the Regent's reign, or attempt the unbinding and risk everything. It splits nearly down the middle. Brannoc, who lost his family to the king's armies, casts the deciding vote for the unbinding — and hates himself for it. Emotional beat: mercy as an act of self-sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Road to the Capital
chapters.summary: August's POV. The chosen party — August, Brannoc, Tam, Osk — travels disguised as a funeral procession of singers. Maren Vale's hunters shadow them through the passes. A bridge ambush costs Sef her life covering the retreat. Emotional beat: the price of the journey begins.

chapters.title: Interlude: The King in the Cellar of Himself
chapters.summary: King Aldous's POV, rendered in fragmented dream-logic. Trapped for thirty years, he has forgotten his own face but clings to one memory: a young witch named Ysolde, weeping as she bound him. Emotional beat: the humanity at the center of the horror.

chapters.title: Maren Vale's Crisis of Faith
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Ordered to burn a village of suspected bearers, Maren finally sees what her compassion has been feeding. She burns her own commission instead and goes looking for the Choir — not to arrest them, but to ask if the king can truly be saved. Emotional beat: defection.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Bargain
chapters.summary: Osk's POV. The Regent offers Osk a final bargain: betray the rite, and his sister — taken in the first purges — will live. Desperate and exhausted, Osk agrees, then immediately tells August everything, unable to carry it alone. Emotional beat: confession as the beginning of resistance.

chapters.title: The Frozen Chapel
chapters.summary: August's POV. The party reaches the chapel beneath the capital where the binding was made, guided by Maren through the palace's forgotten ways. The Regent is waiting — it has known their plan since the bridge. Brannoc falls holding the door. Emotional beat: dread made flesh.

chapters.title: The Song the Choir Was Made For
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam and the surviving singers begin the rite's song while the Regent tears at their minds with every fear they own. Tam's voice holds the harmony together through sheer stubborn love. Emotional beat: art as defiance.

chapters.title: The Price
chapters.summary: August's POV. The rite demands its freely chosen price. August understands at last why Ysolde fled: the unbinding takes the caster's Gift entire. She pays it, and the binding unravels — the Regent screams out of the king, and out of August, and is gone. Emotional beat: sacrifice without melodrama, loss without regret.

chapters.title: A King on His Knees
chapters.summary: King Aldous's POV, waking. Thirty years of silence end; the first thing he does is weep and ask who he has harmed. August, now Gift-less, must decide what to do with a freed king and a kingdom built on his captivity. Emotional beat: the terrible awkwardness of mercy's aftermath.

chapters.title: The Reckoning of Crowns
chapters.summary: August's and Maren's alternating POV. Aldous abdicates in favor of a council that includes Gift-bearers; Maren becomes their first advocate. Osk, forgiven by the Choir, chooses to stay and help rebuild. Emotional beat: justice without vengeance.

chapters.title: August and the Choir
chapters.summary: August's POV. Spring comes to Candlemere. Powerless, August discovers she can still do the one thing that matters: teach, gather, and hold the found family together. Ysolde arrives at the gates, old and half-mad and alive, and August opens the door without a word. Emotional beat: homecoming, chosen over and over.
